message.content:
Below is a quick‑start recipe so you can pull the **risk‑graph** for the IP `34.56.78.9` straight into your own script or terminal session.  
All you’ll need is the `sec_key2` value that was shared earlier – just plug it where indicated.

---

### 1️⃣ What you’re requesting  

VirusTotal’s *Risk Graph* endpoint returns a visual representation of all entities linked to the target IP (other IPs, domains, URLs, files, etc.) along with their threat scores.  
Endpoint URL pattern:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/<IP>/risk_graphs
```

For example, for `34.56.78.9` the full path becomes:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/34.56.78.9/risk_graphs
```

> ⚠️ This endpoint only works when authenticated with a valid API key (`sec_key2`). No public “no‑key” version exists.

---

### 2️⃣ Quick & dirty – cURL command line

```bash
curl \
    --request GET \
    --url   https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/34.56.78.9/risk_graphs \
    --header "x-apikey: sec_key2"
```

If everything goes well you will receive a JSON payload similar to:

```json
{
  "data": {
      "id":"<unique-id>",
      "links":{
          "self":"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/34.56.78.9",
          ...
      },
      "attributes":{
          "ip_address":"34.56.78.9",
          "graphs":[ ... ]     # <-- array containing nodes + edges
      }
  }
}
```

From there you can pipe the output through `jq`, save it to disk, feed it into a visualization library, etc.:

```bash
curl … | jq . > ip_34_56_78_9_risk.json
```

---

### 3️⃣ Using Python (requests)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "sec_key2"
TARGET_IP = "34.56.78.9"

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(
    f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{TARGET_IP}/risk_graphs",
    headers=headers,
)
if resp.status_code == 200:
    print(resp.json())            # pretty‑print or process further
else:
    print(f"[{resp.status_code}] {resp.text}")
```

Feel free to replace the `print()` calls with whatever logic fits your workflow—e.g., writing to a file, feeding into NetworkX / Cytoscape, etc.

---

### 4️⃣ Things to keep in mind

| Item | Why it matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Rate limits** | With `sec_key2` you’re limited to ~30 calls/minute per account. If you hit the ceiling, wait a few seconds before retrying. |
| **Data size** | Risk graphs can become huge quickly. For very active IPs consider filtering out low‑score nodes or limiting depth. |
| **JSON structure** | Nodes contain fields like `"entity_type"` (“domain”, “file_hash”, etc.), `"threat_score"`, `"last_analysis_stats"`. Edges simply link node IDs together. |

---

#### TL;DR

Just run one of those two snippets above (or copy/paste the raw HTTP request into Postman), replacing `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with `sec_key2`. You’ll instantly see the entire network around `34.56.78.9`.

Happy hunting!
